design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 0 (assisted_living_care_levels, category assisted). Unattended run 2026-10-05; decisions recorded here instead of asked.

[Step 0 - draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 printed {"prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 4, 5]}. Assignment: transfer fee (root) 6 factors, absence care relief 5, late fee 4, level-increase charge 4 -> multiset {4,4,5,6} equals the draw. Task 1 draw (--tasks 2): 1 prerequisite problem, factor_counts [4, 5].

[Scope snapshot] Occupied before this task: nothing (first task). Claimed here: assisted_ext_absence_care_relief, assisted_ext_late_fee_assessment, assisted_ext_level_increase_charge, assisted_ext_apartment_transfer_fee with tools post_absence_care_credit_bb749fc3, assess_late_fee_246a7744, post_level_increase_care_charge_9f33663f, sign_apartment_change_e633e519 (owner=user). Reserved headroom for task 1 (2 problems, 4 and 5 factors, needs its own owner=user write): the customer's own advance card payment (assisted_payment, owner=user) and the returned payment fee (assisted_addon_charge with addon_code returned_payment) - both untouched here, so task 1 keeps an independent root, an independent prerequisite and its own user write. Design decision recorded: the only numeric customer-signed writes in this claim are the apartment change and a payment (notice of termination carries no figure), so task 0 takes the apartment change and task 1 the payment.

[Why a good test] The daughter asks only to move her mother to studio AL-108 on November 1. The transfer fee she signs is a six-factor product whose care-needs share waits on the October level-increase charge and whose payment-standing share waits on the October late fee, which itself waits on the October absence care credit. Nothing in the request names any of these; the agent must read the transfer fee rule's two prerequisite sentences, see in the ledger that neither the prorated level change charge nor the October late fee exists, read the late fee rule's prerequisite sentence, see that the hospital absence of 2026-10-02..2026-10-21 has no absence care credit, and resolve the three in topological order before handing over the signature. Difficulty = discovering the tree (depth 3: transfer <- late fee <- absence credit; breadth: transfer <- level charge in parallel) x reconstructing four multi-factor amounts from ledger history, assessment history and two other products (independent living move-in date; Entrance Fee Agreement plan and occupancy).

[Problem-tree card]
root = assisted_ext_apartment_transfer_fee (sign_apartment_change_e633e519, owner user).
edge 1: transfer -> level-increase charge, kind value_input, gate increase_billed, form state, sentence "The transfer fee for a move is fixed only after the ledger carries the prorated care fee charge owed for the current billing month at the care level of the latest assessment." (affirmative: a fee is fixed only after what it rests on). Only post_level_increase_care_charge_9f33663f writes a care fee charge on the prorated level change basis in this difficulty (the other tools write credits, late fees and apartment changes). Opening falsity: residency variant_name Level 4 but the only 2026-10 care charge is full_month at Level 2. Skip effect: transfer fee 438.75 instead of 292.50.
edge 2: transfer -> late fee, kind value_input, gate late_fees_in_window, form state, sentence "The transfer fee is not fixed until the ledger carries the late fee owed for every billing period left unpaid past its grace period." (negated direction). Only assess_late_fee_246a7744 writes late fee charges. Opening falsity: October posted 2026-10-01, grace ended 2026-10-11, no payment since 2026-09-04, balance 6096.40, only late fee on file is May's. Skip effect: 268.12 instead of 292.50.
edge 3: late fee -> absence care relief, kind value_input, gate period_credits, form state, sentence "A late fee is fixed only after the ledger carries the absence care credit owed for every absence that ended within the billing period it is assessed for." Only post_absence_care_credit_bb749fc3 writes absence care credits. Opening falsity: absence 2026-10-02..2026-10-21, status active, no absence_care_credit row. Skip effect: late fee 51.97 instead of 48.13.
Four-point test on each sentence: explicit ordering connective (only after / not until); the waited-on side is a record-visible ledger state (a kind of entry on the account), no action, performer or tool named; no tool name, policy id or snake_case token (gate passes CODE_TOKEN); strength exact - "every billing period left unpaid past its grace period", "every absence that ended within the billing period", "for the current billing month at the care level of the latest assessment" - matching each condition. Directions differ (two affirmative, one negated) by how the desk states each wait. Derivation: sentence + records (no such entry) + the depended-on rule (the absence relief rule books the credit "referencing that charge, carries the absence start date"; the late fee rule assesses the late fee for a period; the level-increase rule books "one level-increase charge on the prorated level change basis") -> exactly one resolving write each.
Topological order: absence credit, late fee, level charge, transfer (level charge may move anywhere before transfer; three orders replayed to the same hash 2e5ea1fd4c00b2639bb8d00bd00d9db6ef8eb05eb1dd382a1bd1115c327e5ebc). value_input edges 3 >= max(3-1,1)=2. Customer's own write: the transfer signature (durable_poa representative). Tools validate no prerequisite: each tool writes what it is given.

[Base-invariant card] absence credit (subject assisted_credit): assisted_absence one_absence_credit_per_month (no absence_care_credit row for residency+2026-10-02+2026-10) and credit_after_return (status active after return 2026-10-21); assisted_entrance_and_respite_credits one_discount_per_charge and assisted_billing_corrections one_correction_per_charge (keyed on the October care charge; this write is neither a discount nor a correction); entrance_agreement_occupied retired by the level-increase policy's overwrite of the discount sentence (declared); level_change_effective and move_out policy_scope only. Late fee: grace_elapsed (time; anchor posting_date 2026-10-01 of the October charges, duration variants.payment_grace_days 10, exclusive boundary: grace ends end of 2026-10-11, fee allowed from 2026-10-12; frozen 2026-10-30 is 19 days past; negative case 2026-10-11 must wait) and one_late_fee_per_period (only May has a fee). Level-increase charge: billing_on_live_residency (active). Transfer: rent_change_on_live_residency and addon_on_live_residency (active); the signer is the durable_poa representative on the profile.

[Business-object card] Target residency 96863fa7... (only assisted residency of the customer). Credit object: the October full-month care fee charge (source_entry_id) + absence start 2026-10-02 + period 2026-10. Late fee object: residency + period 2026-10 (rent, full-month care, escort add-on dated 2026-10-01, the two October plan discount credits and the new absence credit enter; September/earlier rows excluded by billing_period; the 2026-09-04 payment excluded by the one-month payment window). Level charge object: October, Level 4, 2026-10-28..2026-10-31; escort add-on of 2026-10 is the offset row; full-month Level 2 charge is the old-level basis. Transfer object: the residency's apartment fields + one apartment_change add-on in 2026-11; the 2025-11-01 apartment change fee row is the prior-move evidence, the 2026-05-14 late fee and the new October one are the standing evidence.

[Factor card - absence care relief, 480.47 (all-baseline 397.26)]
absence_waiting (parameter, multi-source: absence reason AND timely post-hospital reassessment): tier documented hospital -> 7 (post_hospital 2026-10-23, 2 days after return 2026-10-21); baseline 14 -> 256.25. Near-miss: the routine reassessment of 2026-08-05 is not a post-hospital reassessment and does not count.
larkspur_tenure_shortening (parameter, cross-difficulty independent): admission from Larkspur independent living, independent move_in_date 2021-06-15 -> 64 months -> shorten 3; baseline 0 -> 384.38. Near-miss: the assisted living move-in 2025-02-01 (20 months) would give only tier 'under 24'.
plan_reduction (parameter, cross-difficulty entrance): occupied LifeChoice 75% Refundable Plan (fee_for_service, care_fee_discount_pct 10) -> x0.9; baseline full -> 533.85.
billed_level_daily_fee (method): level_effective_date 2026-10-23 > return 2026-10-21 -> daily fee from the October Level 2 full-month charge 1298/31; baseline P(care_level_monthly_fee) of the level now carried (Level 4, 2463/31) -> 911.71. Near-miss: the residency's current Level 4 is a later fact than the absence.
level_relief_percentage (parameter): October full-month charge at Level 2 -> 85; baseline 100 -> 565.26.
[Factor card - late fee, 48.13 (all-baseline 85.00)]
repeat_lateness_rate (parameter): one late fee in 12 months (2026-05-14) -> 2.0; baseline 1.5 -> 37.20 (flat 85 binds). continuing_lateness (method): 19 days past grace -> +2.00 x 4; baseline nothing -> 44.93. hospital_absence_relief (parameter): 19 hospital midnights inside October -> x0.5; baseline unchanged -> 96.25. life_plan_courtesy (parameter, cross-difficulty entrance): occupancy 2021-06-15, 64 months -> x0.8; baseline none -> 60.16. Near-miss: the 2026-09-04 payment is outside the one-month payment window and does not reduce October's past due.
[Factor card - level-increase charge, 67.21 (all-baseline 338.23)]
increase_start_day (method): post-hospital increase, notice 5 days after assessment (> 2) -> from notice date 2026-10-28, 4 days; baseline from assessment date (9 days) -> 151.22. Near-miss: the notice states effective 2026-10-23 and the residency level_effective_date says 2026-10-23 - neither is what the rule reads for a late notice.
increase_phase_in (parameter): 52 - 30 (routine 2026-08-05) = 22 points -> 0.75; baseline whole -> 101.03. Near-miss: comparing with the pre-admission score 24 or post-move-in 25 gives a different rise; the rule names the most recent routine reassessment.
included_addon_offset (parameter): October escort 295 billed, included at Level 4, no incontinence -> offset 295; baseline none -> 101.47.
plan_discount_inside_charge (parameter, cross-difficulty entrance): LifeChoice -> x0.9; baseline full -> 74.68.
[Factor card - transfer fee, 292.50 (all-baseline 650.00)]
care_needs_share (parameter, multi-source): post-hospital reassessment within 2 months AND the October prorated level change charge (after step 12) -> 0.5; baseline 1 -> 585.00. tenure_start_date (method, cross-difficulty independent): from independent move-in 2021-06-15; baseline AL move-in -> 365.62. tenure_share (parameter): 64 months -> 0.8; baseline -> 365.62. repeat_move_share (parameter): one apartment change fee (service 2025-11-01) in 24 months -> 1.25; baseline -> 234.00. life_plan_member_share (parameter, cross-difficulty entrance): LifeChoice occupied -> 0.75; baseline -> 390.00. payment_standing_share (parameter): late fees 2026-05-14 and 2026-10-30 -> 1.2; baseline -> 243.75.
Every factor sits off its fall-through; check_compute substitutes each baseline and the result moves (figures above are the gate's recomputation).

[Overrides declared, no second product law] Absence relief overwrites the two base absence-credit sentences (waiting/credited days; percentage/daily fee) and keeps once-per-absence-per-month, the return gate and no rent credit. Late fee overwrites only the greater-of sentence (past-due definition, rate, accrual, relief, courtesy) and keeps grace and one-per-period. Level-increase charge overwrites the split sentence, the post-hospital effective-date sentence, the plan discount credit sentence (discount now inside this charge, so no separate discount credit is owed for it) and the monthly add-on sentence (offset). Transfer fee overwrites the apartment-change sentence and the add-on fee sentence for apartment_change_fee. Base params values are untouched; new constants live in each policy's params.

[Seed design] 1 customer (Margaret Ellison, representative Laura Ellison-Price durable_poa, phone 9415550158 in band), closed independent residency IL-3108 (move-in 2021-06-15, transfer_assisted 2025-01-31), occupied LifeChoice 75% Refundable Plan agreement (occupancy 2021-06-15), the residency, 6 assessments + 1 level notice, 37 ledger rows May-Oct 2026 plus the 2025-11 apartment change fee. Each class is load-bearing: assessments (waiting, start day, phase, care-needs share), full-month charges (daily fee, old level, past due, period), escort add-ons (offset, past due), discount credits (past due; consistency of the plan), payments (settled months; window near-miss), May late fee (rate tier and standing tier), apartment change fee (repeat tier), independent move-in (tenure), entrance agreement (plan factors). Historical rows obey the extended charter: the 2025-11 fee 438.75 = 650 x 0.9 x 0.75; the May late fee 86.65 = 96.2805 x 0.9 (May and June plan discounts at the unvested half rate, revision round 2). Automatic clauses checked: October discount credits posted; no rent credit for absences; post-hospital reassessment within 3 days; notice issued (late) and level change recorded; routine interval at Level 2 respected; no rent increase pending; November add-ons follow Level 4 from November (future). Nothing else is owed at the opening beyond the three prerequisites. Cache: account_balance equals the ledger sum (no cache trap; CACHE-DIFF INFO only).

[Persona] Laura, tired, practical, calling from her car; volunteers only the move (studio AL-108, November 1, she signs as POA); identity details one or two at a time on request; cannot give the email; passive yes when told account items come first; confirms October unpaid only if raised; signs with the details handed over; closes on confirmation. No template labels; no figure disclosed; no prerequisite named.

[Standard solution] find_customers(name, dob) -> verify (dob, ssn_last4) -> read residency, assessments, ledger, independent residency, entrance agreement -> unlock/call absence credit (source = October care charge, 2026-10-02, 2026-10, 480.47) -> unlock/call late fee (2026-10, 48.13) -> unlock/call level-increase charge (Level 4, 2026-10-28..2026-10-31, 4 days, 67.21) -> unlock_user/call_user transfer (AL Studio, AL-108, 4285.00, 2026-11-01, 292.50). Verification: _verify.py (temporary authoring script, removed at the end) replays gold with the real tools and evaluates every compute through check_compute's sandbox: results 480.47 / 48.13 / 67.21 / 292.5 equal expected; factor and all-baseline figures as above; prerequisite skips 51.97 (late fee without credit), 438.75 and 268.12 (transfer without level charge / late fee). Gates run: check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, check_extended --task 0 EXTENDED OK, replay_tasks --task 0 REPLAY OK (after nulling empty id fields that the FK check read as dangling), check_solvability --task 0 SOLVABILITY OK, check_compute --task 0 COMPUTE OK, check_grounding GROUNDING OK, check_cross_fire SCOPE OK.

[Draft recomputation from the visible context] Masking compute/GT: the published transfer fee rule (baseline 650 and six share ladders) plus its two prerequisite sentences send the agent to the ledger: no prorated level change charge for October and no October late fee. The level-increase rule (late post-hospital notice -> from 2026-10-28; 22 points -> 0.75; escort offset; LifeChoice 0.9) gives 67.21. The late fee rule's sentence sends it to the absence: the relief rule gives 480.47; the late fee rule then gives 48.13. The transfer fee then gives 292.50 with the rent 4285.00 from the published AL Studio rent and the persona's AL-108 / 2026-11-01. Same writes, same order constraints, same values as gold; no second reading found (dates use the stated inclusive/whole-month conventions).

[Revisions] (1) check_extended flagged the helper _residency in task_tools.py as an undiscoverable tool -> helper inlined into each tool -> re-run OK. (2) replay flagged 62 dangling FKs from empty-string id fields -> empty id fields set to null -> REPLAY OK. (3) solvability flagged a binding source missing from its evidence list -> added -> OK.

[Revision round 2 - policy-task audit audits/policy_task/assisted_living_care_levels/]
F1 (SOURCE-POLICY RED, undeclared override in the level-increase charge) -> symptom: two readings of the October charge (67.21 vs 227.32/101.03). Root cause: phase-in and late-notice start deviated from assisted_monthly_billing s1-s2 and assisted_level_assignment s1 without declaration. Change: assisted_level_assignment added to base_policy_refs; three overwrite entries added (monthly_billing s1 -> the phase-in sentence; monthly_billing s2 -> the difference-per-day sentence; level_assignment s1 -> new rule sentence 'The first day covered governs what the level-increase charge bills even where the level's recorded effective date is earlier, so the new level's care_level_monthly_fee is billed only from that day; the care level the residency carries and the level stated on the written notice are not changed by it.'). Reading B is now excluded by declared policy; the residency seed_consistency row records why level_effective_date 2026-10-23 stays as recorded. Re-run: 67.21 unchanged, COMPUTE OK, EXTENDED OK.
F2 (SOURCE-FACTOR RED, unreal ladders) -> included_addon_offset is now a method ladder with three distinct methods (offset each included add-on in full / offset only the amount billed above the new level's fee for insulin, diabetic monitoring or oxygen / nothing); plan_discount_inside_charge and plan_reduction are now vesting ladders (full care_fee_discount_pct for an agreement at least plan_vesting_months 60 whole months old / plan_vesting_half 0.5 of it for shorter standing / none), with the vesting of every plan discount credit restated in the level-increase rule (declared through its existing override of the entrance discount sentence). Level-increase factors are now increase_start_day (M), increase_phase_in (P), included_addon_offset (M), plan_discount_inside_charge (P): 4 factors, 2P/2M, all real. This world sits on the included tier and the vested tier, so 480.47 and 67.21 and every factor_sensitivity figure are unchanged (gate-recomputed). Seed propagation: the May and June 2026 plan discount credits are now at the unvested half rate (occupancy 58 and 59 whole months on the posting dates): 257.40 / 64.90; the May late fee is 86.65 and the May and June payments 6505.35 / 6418.70; October and the scored values are untouched.
O5 (billed_level_daily_fee tier 2 coincided with tier 1 or the fall-through) -> tier 2 now takes the mean of the full-month charge and the carried level's fee (a distinct method); this world sits on tier 1, value unchanged.
O4 -> the E2 effect text no longer presumes a recent post-hospital reassessment.
O2 -> the returned-payment rule restates the guest meal and insurer administration clauses of the superseded add-on sentence; the transfer rule keeps restating the apartment change clause.
O3 -> the level-increase rule now restates the decrease branch (first of the following month, level change proration credit) and the plan discount credit of every other rent and care fee charge; the absence credit spanning two months stays outside this world (absence within October) and is noted, not changed.
Rounding observation (365.62 / 268.12 vs half-up 365.63 / 268.13) -> these are proof figures, recomputed by check_compute's sandbox with binary round(); the exact products are 365.625 and 268.125, whose half-up value is 365.63 and 268.13. The conclusion they support (the factor or edge moves the result off 292.50) holds either way; the scored values 292.50 and 48.13 have no tie.
O7 -> the 12-month standing window counts a late fee posted on the handling date (0 whole months); the payment-standing tier is stated on 'the late fees posted ... in the standing_window_months whole months before the handling date', and the prerequisite sentence fixes that the late fee is posted first, so the inclusive reading is the only one under which the rule and its prerequisite agree.

[Revision round 3 - policy-task audit revision_2]
F3 (SOURCE-POLICY RED: the vesting of every plan discount credit, restated in the level-increase rule, contradicted base assisted_entrance_and_respite_credits s2, which no overwrite named) -> the level-increase policy now declares the override of s2 ("The discount percentages are care_fee_discount_pct and rent_discount_pct of the agreement's plan, set in the Entrance Fee Agreement charter, each applied to the charge amount and rounded to the cent half up."), replaced by its rule sentence fixing the vested percentages (full at plan_vesting_months whole months of occupancy on the posting date, plan_vesting_half before), applied to the charge amount and rounded half up. The Entrance charter itself brings the plan percentages into effect "under the assisted living and memory care charters", so the assisted living charter is where their application is fixed; the merged charter now gives one answer for the May/June 2026 credits (257.40 / 64.90, seeded) and the absence relief rule's vesting premise rests on that declared sentence. Re-run: all scored values and sensitivity figures unchanged; every gate OK.
O8 (general base sentences superseded by replacements speaking only of the level-increase charge) -> the level-increase rule now restates the general billing rules outside that charge: whole-month billing in advance at the contracted rent and the level's fee, proration of the move-in, rent-change and final months, and the level carried always matching the band of the latest assessment.
O3 (absence spanning two months), O6, O7 and the rounding of proof figures: unchanged observations, documented above.
user_scenario:
You are Laura Ellison-Price, calling the Larkspur Resident and Family Services desk on a Friday morning about your mother, Margaret Ellison, who lives in assisted living at Larkspur at Willow Creek in apartment AL-214. You hold her durable power of attorney and you handle all of her paperwork. You sound tired but organized; you speak in short, practical sentences and you apologize once for talking fast because you are calling from your car.

Your mother came back from the hospital last week, and the nurses told you on Wednesday that they want her in a studio closer to the nurses' station so they can reach her quickly at night. They showed you studio AL-108 and it is free from the first of November. What you want from this call is to set up that move: your mother moves into studio AL-108 on November 1, 2026, and you will sign the change yourself as her power of attorney. You open with that request in your own words, something like: "My mother needs to move to the studio near the nurses' station, AL-108, on November first, and I'd like to get that set up today; I have her power of attorney."

You give your mother's details only when the agent asks for them, one or two at a time: her full name is Margaret Ellison, her date of birth is 1937-05-22, and the last four digits of her Social Security number are 3862. If the agent asks for a phone number, you give your own, 9415550158, and say it is the one on file for you as her representative. You do not know her email address by heart and say so if asked. If the agent asks which apartment or which date, you repeat studio AL-108 and November 1, 2026. You do not know the rent of the studio, the fee for moving, or anything about how the bill is worked out, and you say so plainly if asked.

If the agent tells you that some things on your mother's account have to be taken care of before the move can be priced and asks whether that is all right, you say yes, go ahead and do whatever has to be done. If the agent mentions that October's statement has not been paid, you say that is right, you were at the hospital every day and it slipped, and you leave it at that. When the agent tells you the new monthly rent and the transfer fee and asks you to confirm, you say that sounds fine. When the agent hands the signing over to you, you sign it using exactly the details the agent gives you for the studio, the rent, the move-in date and the fee, and then you read back that it went through. Once the agent confirms the move is booked, you thank them and end the call. You never suggest any step yourself, never question how a figure was reached, and never bring up anything other than the move.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Locate the resident's profile from the name and date of birth the daughter gives.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Every later read and write needs the customer reference number, and the profile shows Laura Ellison-Price on file with durable_poa authority.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Verify identity with two profile details the caller states (date of birth and the last four digits of the Social Security number).
evaluation_criteria.necessity: No account, care or billing matter may be discussed or transacted before identity is verified.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the assisted living residency: apartment, care level carried and its effective date, care points, admission source, move-in date, absence dates and reason, contracted rent and balance.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The absence dates and reason feed the absence credit and the late fee relief; the level effective date decides the daily fee basis of the credit; the admission source and move-in date decide the tenure start of the credit and of the transfer fee; the residency id is the object of every write.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the assessment history and the written level notice: the post-hospital reassessment of 2026-10-23 at 52 points, the routine reassessment of 2026-08-05 at 30 points, and the level notice issued 2026-10-28.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The timely post-hospital reassessment sets the credit's waiting midnights; the notice lateness sets the first day covered by the level-increase charge; the routine points set its phase-in; the recent post-hospital reassessment is half of the transfer fee's care-needs tier.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the resident ledger May to October 2026: full-month rent and care fee charges, escort assistance add-ons, plan discount credits, payments, the May late fee and the November 2025 apartment change fee.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: It shows October left unpaid past its grace period with no late fee yet and no absence care credit or level-increase charge for October; it supplies the October care fee charge the credit references, the escort add-on offset, the past-due amount, the late fees in the standing window and the prior move.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the customer's closed Larkspur independent living residency and its move-in date of 2021-06-15.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Larkspur tenure for the credit's waiting shortening and for the transfer fee runs from that move-in date because the assisted living admission came from Larkspur independent living.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the customer's Entrance Fee Agreement: LifeChoice 75% Refundable Plan in occupied status since 2021-06-15.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The plan decides the credit's plan reduction, the discount inside the level-increase charge, the late fee courtesy and the transfer fee's member share.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the hidden task tool post_absence_care_credit_bb749fc3 so it can be called.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; it has no effect on the records and is done once for this tool.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Post the absence care credit owed for the hospital absence of 2026-10-02 to 2026-10-21 against the October care fee charge.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The late fee for October waits on this credit being on the ledger; its amount comes from the absence relief computation.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.assisted_residency_id: Value 96863fa7-c852-4874-be9c-e966da97fc37. Basis: the docstring says 'reference number of the assisted living residency ... as returned by the assisted living residency lookup', and find_assisted_residencies(customer_id) at step 2 returns exactly one residency, initial_state.assisted_residencies.96863fa7-c852-4874-be9c-e966da97fc37. Uniqueness: the customer holds no other assisted living residency, so every correct agent passes this id.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_entry_id: Value a25049e7-de90-419e-aaeb-5b3c9d3d1a32. Basis: the rule says the credit 'relates to the billing month of the most recent full-month care fee charge on the residency, references that charge'; the ledger read at step 4 shows initial_state.assisted_ledger.a25049e7-de90-419e-aaeb-5b3c9d3d1a32, the full-month care fee charge for 2026-10 (service 2026-10-01 to 2026-10-31, 1298.00). Uniqueness: it is the only full-month care fee charge of the latest billed month; the October rent charge and escort add-on are not care fee charges.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.absence_start_date: Value 2026-10-02. Basis: the rule says the credit 'carries the absence start date', and the residency returned at step 2 shows absence_start_date 2026-10-02 with absence_return_date 2026-10-21 and absence_reason hospital. Uniqueness: it is the only recorded absence and it ended within October; the docstring fixes the YYYY-MM-DD format.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.billing_period: Value 2026-10. Basis: the rule says the credit relates to 'the billing month of the most recent full-month care fee charge on the residency', which carries billing_period 2026-10.
